title: Model Fallout Sentinel: cross-region fallback scoring & procurement trigger POC
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: when external model providers experience regional outages, latency spikes, or pricing shocks, product teams at Redwood need an automated, auditable way to: (1) detect outage/quality signals across regions, (2) score candidate fallback models by compatibility/cost/latency, and (3) trigger procurement or reserved-capacity workflows (for Dedicated/Private) with minimal human friction.

This ticket is a product POC for a Model Fallout Sentinel: a signal fusion pipeline + dashboard + runbook that automates fallback scoring and surfaces procurement triggers. The goal is to reduce manual emergency provisioning time from hours to minutes and to bake predictable procurement thresholds into the Console and internal ops flows.

Scope for POC:
- Define signal taxonomy (latency, error-rate, rate-limit, price-change, model-deprecation-announcement).
- Implement prototype signal aggregator that pulls telemetry from Hosted API, Dedicated metrics, and public model-provider feeds (scraped/partner APIs).
- Build a compatibility scoring heuristic: semantic equivalence (embedding/LM profile), token-cost delta, expected latency delta (region-aware), and fallback risk.
- Surface top-3 fallback options per customer/route in a Console mock and internal incident dashboard.
- Define procurement trigger rules (score threshold + cost delta + customer SLA tier) and wire to a gated automation (Slack + Procurement runbook).

Out of scope for POC: full procurement billing automation, multi-tenant quota enforcement, in-depth legal/vendor onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy documented and approved by Eng + SRE + PM.
Prototype aggregator ingests at least three distinct signal sources (hosted metrics, Dedicated telemetry, and public provider status) and normalizes them to a common event model.
Compatibility scoring prototype returns ranked fallback models for sample routes with explainability labels (why chosen, expected cost delta, confidence score).
A Console mock (Figma) and internal dashboard show the top-3 fallback options for two real customer routes and a simulated APAC outage.
Procurement trigger playbook documented with gated approvals (Slack channel + on-call ping) and an example manual trigger tested by ops.
POC write-up includes clear next steps for productionization (end-to-end automation, security review, procurement policy updates).
steps_progress: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with Eng runtime, SRE, and Procurement. Agreed on high-level signal sources and initial success metrics.

2026-02-19: Prototype signal schema v0.1 defined (latency_p95, err_rate_5m, throttled_5m, price_delta_pct, provider_announcement). Saved to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Model+Fallout+Sentinel+Schema

2026-02-26: Eng implemented ingestion adapter for Hosted API metrics (pull from telemetry API). First normalized events visible in test dashboard (Grafana): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/fallout-sentinel/proto

2026-03-03: Scoring heuristic draft completed. Uses model-compat table (embedding vector affinity), token-cost estimator, and region latency multiplier. Shared for review: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1scoring-draft
2026-03-09: Figma mock of Console panel (top-3 fallbacks + explainability) linked in ticket and reviewed by Design. Mock: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Model-Fallout-Sentinel
2026-03-11: Procurement reviewed trigger thresholds. Requested addition of manual approval gate for Reserved capacity > $5K/month.
2026-03-12: Decision to instrument a synthetic APAC outage test next week and capture time-to-fallback and end-to-end logs for runbook refinement.
decisions: Use a scoring heuristic (0-100) rather than binary pass/fail to allow tiered automation (autofallback for score>85, ops-gated for 60-85, manual for <60).
Prototype will only surface procurement triggers; billing automation deferred to a separate procurement engineering ticket.
Compatibility checks will prioritize embedding and generative-behavior deltas over model architecture equivalence to reduce false negatives.
Signal sources prioritized: Hosted telemetry (high confidence), Dedicated telemetry (high confidence), provider status feeds (medium), public price scrapes (low initially).
notes:
Trade-offs: tighter automation reduces time-to-recover but increases risk of unexpected vendor spend and model-quality regressions. POC will instrument strong simulation/tests and require an ops approval gate for high-cost routes.

Next steps: run synthetic APAC outage (owner: Liam), capture metrics for 3 customer routes, refine scoring weights with SRE, and prepare productionization PRD by 2026-03-25.
